posts.raw_content:
They didn’t turn Trump’s executive orders into law. They didn’t pass the SAVE America Act. The RINO coalition fought Trump and blocked the people’s will at every turn.

Congressional Republicans talked tough about corrupt Democrats but took no meaningful action. Meanwhile, Democrats went after Trump’s allies, and Steve Bannon and Peter Navarro ended up in prison. Republicans never moved beyond tough talk, even against the most corrupt of their enemies.
Worse, they did things like join Democrats to kick George Santos out of Congress. Where was that same determination against a truly bad person like immigration (and other) fraudster Ilhan Omar, who still holds her seat?
By every metric, they let the American people down. Now they have to pay. Unfortunately, the rest of us pay, too. 

Is America (as a great nation) coming to an end? I don’t think we’re there yet... but we did just take a 'Great Leap Forward' (in the Mao sense).

None of this is to say Democrats aren’t bad. They are. We are already under threat, with a charismatic and hateful radical socialist leading America’s largest city and a growing communist movement in the DSA. As of tonight, we have a creepy, open-borders man-boy in Texas and an America-hating, antisemitic socialist faux-doctor, El-Sayed, in Michigan poised to rule over us... all because the GOP doesn’t know how to win or even seem to want to.
Rush Limbaugh used to say establishment Republicans preferred being the controlled opposition to being the party that leads. I think he was right again. Republicans would rather play by the Marquess of Queensberry rules, no matter how savage the opposition. Trump tried to teach them to fight back. They balked. Time after time, they acted against the will of their voters. They still do.

Trump, the eternal optimist, quixotically tried to push them toward greatness. They refused to answer the call. Will this smackdown be the wake-up call they need? We can only hope so.

Every time an authentic outsider challenges the establishment, conservative voters answer the call: Buchanan in ’92, the Tea Party, and most recently Donald Trump and MAGA. Voters hand the GOP victory after victory, only for those elected to look that gift horse in the mouth. Then, like the townspeople in Shane, they decide the man who saved them is too uncouth for their delicate sensibilities.

Having said that, as great as Trump has been (overall), it was a strategic error to get into a war with Iran before the midterms, and perhaps less than wise to partner with Israel in doing so. Eight months in, it’s too early to tell whether it will turn out to have been a wise move... but even if it goes down as a win, it still cost him support.

Of course, not all of America threw away the chance to be great. States like Florida that resisted the siren song of socialism and stayed red will thrive economically.

Still, the bigger picture looks grim. The stock market is already crashing, and the economy at large will soon follow. It might be a good time to liquidate and start saving for the hard times ahead.
